  Plan your boat day

  Private vs shared boat toursWhen a private boat is worth it, and when a shared tour is the smart choice.Boat tours from PositanoCapri, sunset cruises and private boats leaving from Positano beach.Boat tours from AmalfiCapri day trips and private coast cruises from Amalfi harbour.Boat tours from SorrentoThe shortest way to Capri, plus boat days to Positano and Amalfi.Capri & the Blue Grotto by boatHow the Blue Grotto really works, and how to avoid disappointment.Boat tours with kidsWhich boat days work with children, and what to pack.Boat tour pricesWhat boat tours cost in 2027 and what drives the price.When to goBest months, best time of day and what happens if the weather turns.

  Two routes, many listings

Search for a boat tour here and you get hundreds of results. Strip away the photos and almost all of them follow one of two routes.

The first goes west to Capri. You pass Li Galli, the three small islands Nureyev once owned, round Punta Campanella and spend the morning circling Capri: the Faraglioni (the boat usually goes through the arch in the middle one), the Green and White grottoes, the lighthouse at Punta Carena and, if the sea allows, the Blue Grotto. Then a few hours ashore at Marina Grande.

The second stays on the coast. Positano from the water, Praiano, the fjord at Furore with its bridge, the Emerald Grotto, Amalfi and tiny Atrani next door. Shorter, calmer, more swimming.

After that it comes down to who is on board and how long you have. Two people on a budget are fine on a shared boat. A family of five, or anyone celebrating something, should at least get a price for a private gozzo. It is often closer than people expect.

About the scores

We score tour types, not individual listings, using the criteria on our method page. We do not write reviews. The customer ratings you see in the GetYourGuide boxes come from their verified bookings.

Frequently asked questions
What is the best boat tour on the Amalfi Coast?
For most first-time visitors, a small-group Capri boat tour from Positano gives the best mix of sights, swim stops and price. Families and groups of six or more usually do better with a private boat. See our full ranking.
How much does a boat tour on the Amalfi Coast cost?
Shared full-day tours to Capri typically cost €80–180 per person depending on the starting town and season. Private boats start around €450 for a few hours on the coast and reach €900–2,200 per boat for a full day to Capri. Details in our price guide.
Do boat tours to Capri include the Blue Grotto?
Most stop outside the Blue Grotto when it is open, but entry is by small rowing boats and is paid separately on the spot. It closes in rough seas, so no tour can guarantee it.
Can I book a custom boat tour?
Yes. Message us on WhatsApp (+39 393 855 2086) with your dates and group size and we will suggest options, including private boats.

Want a tailor-made boat day?
Send us your dates, how many you are and where you are staying. We answer on WhatsApp, and we also know a few skippers who do not sell online.

  Ask on WhatsApp

Scores out of 10 are editorial judgements based on routes, inclusions, typical group sizes and prices across listings, weighted as explained on our method page. They are not customer reviews.

  #1 Private boat tour to Capri 8.8

  Best for: couples, families and groups of 4 to 10

  A private day follows the same basic route as the shared tours, but the skipper adapts it to you: longer swims at the Faraglioni, lunch at a beach club in Marina Piccola or Anacapri, an early start to beat the queue at the Blue Grotto. Departures are possible from Positano, Amalfi, Praiano or Sorrento.
Price depends mostly on the boat. A traditional wooden gozzo with a sun canopy is the classic choice, a speedboat is faster and better from Amalfi, a yacht costs considerably more. Split between six or eight people, a gozzo is often not much more per head than a shared tour.
Ask your skipper about lunch near Bagni di Tiberio, west of Marina Grande, where you swim next to the remains of a Roman villa.

  What works
- Completely flexible itinerary
- Best for families, honeymoons and groups
- Skipper doubles as a local guide

  Before you book
- Fuel and port fees may be extra
- Clarify what drinks and food are included
- Book early for July and August

  From: Positano, Amalfi, Sorrento · 6–8 h · €900–2,200 per boat

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia GetYourGuide

  #2 Capri boat tour from Positano (shared) 8.6

  Best for: first-time visitors staying in Positano

  Boats leave from the pier on Positano's main beach in the morning, pass the Li Galli islands and cross to Capri past Punta Campanella. Most of the morning is a slow lap of the island: the Faraglioni rocks and the arch, the green and white grottoes, the Punta Carena lighthouse, and a stop outside the Blue Grotto if it is open. You then get two to four hours ashore at Marina Grande to ride the funicular up to the Piazzetta or have lunch, before sailing back in the late afternoon.
Small-group boats (roughly 10 to 15 people) are noticeably more pleasant than large ones. Drinks and snorkelling gear are often included, lunch on Capri usually is not.
A small detail people miss: the three Li Galli islands were bought by the dancer Léonide Massine in the 1920s and later by Rudolf Nureyev. They are still private, so you see them from the boat only.

  What works
- Covers almost every Capri highlight in one day
- Positano is close enough to Capri for an easy crossing
- Several swim stops in clear water
- Good value per person

  Before you book
- Blue Grotto entry is extra and depends on the sea
- Free time on Capri is busy in July and August
- Large boats mean less flexibility

  From: Positano · 7–8 h · €95–170 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia GetYourGuide

  #3 Private Amalfi Coast boat tour (half or full day) 8.5

  Best for: families and anyone who prefers swimming to sightseeing

  Without the crossing to Capri, a private boat can spend its time on the coast itself: the tiny beach of Atrani, the Emerald Grotto at Conca dei Marini, the Furore fjord and its bridge, the coves of Praiano, Positano from the sea and the Li Galli islands. Many people book three or four hours, ending with a swim before sunset.
It is the calmest boat option and the easiest with young children, because you can stop and turn back whenever you like.
The Emerald Grotto was found by a local fisherman in 1932, and there is a ceramic nativity scene on the seabed inside. The bridge over the Furore fjord is about 30 metres high and is used for diving competitions in summer.

  What works
- Calm water and short distances
- Flexible length, from 3 hours
- Ideal for swimming and young children

  Before you book
- Emerald Grotto visit has its own ticket
- Shorter tours cover only part of the coast
- Check whether fuel is included

  From: Positano, Amalfi · 3–8 h · €450–1,500 per boat

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia Viator

  #4 Positano sunset boat tour 8.4

  Best for: couples and anyone with only one evening

  Short evening cruises leave Positano in the late afternoon, sail toward the Li Galli islands for a swim and return as the sun drops behind the coast, so you see Positano light up from the water. Most include a glass of prosecco or limoncello and snacks.
It is the best boat option if you only have an evening, and an easy first time on a boat for children or anyone unsure about seasickness.
In early summer the sun goes down behind the ridge toward Sorrento rather than into the sea. The real show is the light turning the houses pink and orange.

  What works
- Short and easy to fit in
- Best light of the day
- Good introduction for children

  Before you book
- Exact sunset view depends on the season
- Shared versions can feel crowded
- Not a sightseeing tour

  From: Positano · 2–3 h · €50–95 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia GetYourGuide

  #5 Capri boat tour from Sorrento (shared) 8.4

  Best for: travellers based in Sorrento or arriving from Naples

  Sorrento is the closest base to Capri, so the crossing from Marina Piccola past the Sorrento peninsula takes well under an hour. That leaves more of the day for the island lap, the swim stops and free time ashore. Many boats also pass the Bay of Ieranto and the Punta Campanella marine reserve.
Because Sorrento has more tour operators, the choice is wider and prices are a little lower. Pick a small group and check whether the hotel pickup or the meeting point at the harbour is included.
The Bay of Ieranto, just before Punta Campanella, is protected and looked after by the FAI, the Italian National Trust. It is one of the clearest swims in the area when the boat stops there.

  What works
- Shortest crossing, more time on Capri
- Widest choice of operators
- Often the lowest price per person

  Before you book
- Does not show the Amalfi Coast itself
- Busy harbour in high season
- Check pickup arrangements

  From: Sorrento · 7–8 h · €80–150 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia GetYourGuide

  #6 Capri island boat tour & Blue Grotto (from Capri) 8.4

  Best for: day trippers already on Capri

  If you reach Capri by ferry, the cheapest way to see it from the sea is a round-the-island trip from Marina Grande. In one to two hours you pass the Blue Grotto, the Punta Carena lighthouse, the coves of the south coast and the Faraglioni. Some operators let you get off at the Blue Grotto to join the queue for the rowing boats.
Comfort varies a lot: shared boats can be crowded, so small-group or private versions are worth the extra in summer.
The Blue Grotto was known to the Romans, then mostly avoided by locals for centuries. It became famous after the German writer August Kopisch wrote about it in 1826.

  What works
- Cheapest way to see Capri by sea
- Short, easy to combine with a day on the island
- Option to stop at the Blue Grotto

  Before you book
- You need to reach Capri first, by ferry
- Few or no swim stops
- Busy boats at midday in summer

  From: Capri (Marina Grande) · 1–2 h · €20–45 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia Viator

  #7 Capri boat tour from Amalfi (shared) 8.1

  Best for: travellers based in Amalfi, Ravello or Minori

  From Amalfi the boat first runs west along the coast past Conca dei Marini, Praiano and Positano, so you see the coast from the water before even reaching Capri. Expect about an hour and a half of sailing each way. On Capri the programme is similar to tours from Positano: a lap of the island with swim stops, the Blue Grotto if open, and free time ashore.
It is the right choice if you are staying in Amalfi, Atrani, Ravello or Minori and want Capri without first travelling to Positano. If you are flexible, starting from Positano shortens the day.
On the way west, look up at Praiano: the majolica dome of San Gennaro is one of the brightest things on the coast in morning light.

  What works
- Sees the whole coastline from the sea
- No need to travel to Positano first
- Usually includes swim stops on both legs

  Before you book
- Longest day of all the shared tours
- More time sailing, slightly less on Capri
- Afternoon return can be choppy

  From: Amalfi · 8–9 h · €100–180 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia Viator

  #8 Amalfi Coast boat tour from Sorrento (Positano & Amalfi) 8.0

  Best for: Sorrento guests who want to see Positano and Amalfi

  The boat rounds Punta Campanella and follows the coast east past Nerano and the Li Galli islands to Positano, where you usually get time ashore, then continues past Praiano and the Furore fjord to Amalfi for lunch and a visit to the cathedral. The return follows the same route with a swim stop.
It replaces the famous but crowded coast road with a far more relaxing day, and it is the best way to see Positano's cliffside houses from the angle in every photo.
From the sea you get the full view of Positano's church of Santa Maria Assunta and its green and yellow tiled dome, which is hard to see properly from the lanes.

  What works
- Avoids the traffic on the coast road
- Time ashore in Positano and Amalfi
- Postcard views from the water

  Before you book
- Long sailing time if the sea is choppy
- Does not include Capri
- Short stops if the boat runs late

  From: Sorrento · 7–8 h · €90–160 per person

  Route map & details
  Book nowvia Viator

If you just want an answer

- First time here, normal budget: a shared Capri trip from wherever you are staying.

- Kids, a group of six or more, or a special occasion: a private boat. Capri if you have the whole day, the coast if you do not.

- Only one free evening: the sunset trip out of Positano.

- Already on Capri for the day: the round-the-island boat from Marina Grande, then lunch.

Frequently asked questions
Are these rankings based on reviews?
No. They are editorial scores built on five published criteria. Customer ratings appear separately in the GetYourGuide listings, which come from verified bookings.
Is Capri or the Amalfi Coast better by boat?
Capri has the more famous sights (Faraglioni, Blue Grotto) and lets you go ashore. The coast route is calmer, shorter and better for swimming in quiet coves. With one day, most people choose Capri.
Which tour is best for a honeymoon?
A private boat, either a full day to Capri or a half day along the coast ending at sunset off Positano.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/about/

Home / How we rateHow we rate boat tours
amalficoastboatguide.com is a small independent site. We are not a tour operator and we do not own boats. We put this together because booking a boat day here is more confusing than it should be: the same trip is sold under dozens of names at very different prices.

What we score

Listings change every week, so we do not score them one by one. We score the eight kinds of trip that actually exist on the Amalfi Coast and around Capri, looking at the route, what is usually included, typical group size and the prices we see across many listings. Each kind gets a mark out of 10 on five criteria, and a fixed weighting turns those into one score.

Reviews

We do not write or invent customer reviews. Customer ratings on this site come only from GetYourGuide's live listings, which are tied to real bookings.

Money

Some links are affiliate links to GetYourGuide and Viator. If you book through them we may earn a commission and you pay the same price. That does not change our scores. Photos come from Unsplash or from our partners' widgets.

Something wrong?

Prices and rules here change every season. If you spot something out of date, send us a WhatsApp and we will correct it.
Our five criteria
- Scenery (30%): how many of the coast's headline sights the route actually reaches, and how close the boat can get.
- Value (25%): what you get for the typical price: hours on the water, swim stops, drinks, free time.
- Time well spent (20%): share of the day spent seeing things rather than transferring, queuing or waiting.
- Comfort (15%): group size, shade, seating, flexibility of the plan and how rough the crossing usually is.
- Families (10%): suitability for children: duration, shade, freedom to adapt stops, safety gear.

  Sorrento is the closest base to Capri, so the crossing from Marina Piccola past the Sorrento peninsula takes well under an hour. That leaves more of the day for the island lap, the swim stops and free time ashore. Many boats also pass the Bay of Ieranto and the Punta Campanella marine reserve.
Because Sorrento has more tour operators, the choice is wider and prices are a little lower. Pick a small group and check whether the hotel pickup or the meeting point at the harbour is included.
The Bay of Ieranto, just before Punta Campanella, is protected and looked after by the FAI, the Italian National Trust. It is one of the clearest swims in the area when the boat stops there.

  What works
- Shortest crossing, more time on Capri
- Widest choice of operators
- Often the lowest price per person

  Before you book
- Does not show the Amalfi Coast itself
- Busy harbour in high season
- Check pickup arrangements

  The boat rounds Punta Campanella and follows the coast east past Nerano and the Li Galli islands to Positano, where you usually get time ashore, then continues past Praiano and the Furore fjord to Amalfi for lunch and a visit to the cathedral. The return follows the same route with a swim stop.
It replaces the famous but crowded coast road with a far more relaxing day, and it is the best way to see Positano's cliffside houses from the angle in every photo.
From the sea you get the full view of Positano's church of Santa Maria Assunta and its green and yellow tiled dome, which is hard to see properly from the lanes.

  What works

  A private day follows the same basic route as the shared tours, but the skipper adapts it to you: longer swims at the Faraglioni, lunch at a beach club in Marina Piccola or Anacapri, an early start to beat the queue at the Blue Grotto. Departures are possible from Positano, Amalfi, Praiano or Sorrento.
Price depends mostly on the boat. A traditional wooden gozzo with a sun canopy is the classic choice, a speedboat is faster and better from Amalfi, a yacht costs considerably more. Split between six or eight people, a gozzo is often not much more per head than a shared tour.
Ask your skipper about lunch near Bagni di Tiberio, west of Marina Grande, where you swim next to the remains of a Roman villa.

  What works
- Completely flexible itinerary
- Best for families, honeymoons and groups
- Skipper doubles as a local guide

  Before you book

- Clarify what drinks and food are included
- Book early for July and August

- Amalfi

  Without the crossing to Capri, a private boat can spend its time on the coast itself: the tiny beach of Atrani, the Emerald Grotto at Conca dei Marini, the Furore fjord and its bridge, the coves of Praiano, Positano from the sea and the Li Galli islands. Many people book three or four hours, ending with a swim before sunset.
It is the calmest boat option and the easiest with young children, because you can stop and turn back whenever you like.
The Emerald Grotto was found by a local fisherman in 1932, and there is a ceramic nativity scene on the seabed inside. The bridge over the Furore fjord is about 30 metres high and is used for diving competitions in summer.

  What works
- Calm water and short distances
- Flexible length, from 3 hours
- Ideal for swimming and young children

  Before you book
- Emerald Grotto visit has its own ticket
- Shorter tours cover only part of the coast
- Check whether fuel is included

- Capri (Marina Grande)
- Faraglioni rocks
- Marina Piccola

- Capri (Marina Grande)

  If you reach Capri by ferry, the cheapest way to see it from the sea is a round-the-island trip from Marina Grande. In one to two hours you pass the Blue Grotto, the Punta Carena lighthouse, the coves of the south coast and the Faraglioni. Some operators let you get off at the Blue Grotto to join the queue for the rowing boats.
Comfort varies a lot: shared boats can be crowded, so small-group or private versions are worth the extra in summer.
The Blue Grotto was known to the Romans, then mostly avoided by locals for centuries. It became famous after the German writer August Kopisch wrote about it in 1826.

  What works
- Cheapest way to see Capri by sea
- Short, easy to combine with a day on the island
- Option to stop at the Blue Grotto

- Busy boats at midday in summer

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/private-vs-shared-boat-tour-amalfi-coast/

Home / Guides / Private vs shared boat tours
Private vs shared boat tour on the Amalfi Coast

Most people decide this first, and it changes everything else about the day.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

Choose a shared small-group tour if you are one to three people on a normal budget. Choose a private boat for families with young children, groups of six or more, special occasions or if you want to control the timing.

The real difference

Both follow similar routes. What changes is who decides. On a shared tour the plan is fixed: departure time, swim stops, time ashore. On a private boat the skipper works for you, so you can leave early to beat the crowds at the Blue Grotto, stay longer at a cove you like or skip Capri town entirely.

Cost per person

GroupShared Capri tourPrivate gozzo to Capri

2 people€190–340 total€900–2,200 total

4 people€380–680 total€225–550 each

8 people€760–1,360 total€115–275 each

Indicative ranges. From around six people, a private boat is often close to the shared price per head.

Choose shared if

- you are travelling alone, as a couple or as a small group on a budget;
- you enjoy meeting other travellers;
- you are happy with a set plan.

Choose private if

- you have children who need shade, snacks and shorter stretches;
- it is a honeymoon, proposal or birthday;
- you want a specific beach club lunch or an early Blue Grotto attempt;
- you are six or more.

What to check before booking either

Group size (small group means roughly 12 or fewer), what drinks and snorkel gear are included, whether fuel and port fees are extra on private boats, and the cancellation policy for bad weather.

Frequently asked questions
Is a private boat tour on the Amalfi Coast worth the money?
For groups of six or more, families and special occasions, usually yes: per person it costs little more than shared seats and the day is far more flexible.
How many people fit on a private gozzo?
Typical gozzo boats take 8 to 12 passengers. Larger groups need a bigger boat or two boats.
Can I share a private boat with strangers?
Some operators sell seats on small "semi-private" boats. Ask us on WhatsApp if you want to be matched.

Want a tailor-made boat day?
Send us your dates, how many you are and where you are staying. We answer on WhatsApp, and we also know a few skippers who do not sell online.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/boat-tours-from-positano/

Home / Guides / Boat tours from Positano
Boat tours from Positano

Positano is the most popular base for boat days, with tours leaving straight from the beach.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

From Positano the best full-day option is a small-group Capri boat tour: 7 to 8 hours, about 45 to 60 minutes each way, usually €95–170 per person. With only an evening, take the sunset cruise to Li Galli (€50–95). Groups and families should price a private gozzo, roughly €900–2,200 per boat.

Where boats leave from

Almost all tours start from the pier on Spiaggia Grande, the main beach, a short walk down from the centre. Operators have kiosks along the beach. Arrive 15 minutes early; in summer the pier is busy and boats leave on time.

Your options

- Shared Capri day (7–8 hours): the most booked tour in the area. See route and details.

- Sunset cruise (2–3 hours): Li Galli, a swim and an aperitivo. Details.

- Private boat to Capri: same route, your pace. Details.

- Private coast cruise: Praiano, Furore and the Emerald Grotto in a half day. Details.

Capri boat tour from Positano: how the day goes

Boarding is usually between 9 and 10 in the morning at the Spiaggia Grande pier. The boat stops for a swim off the Li Galli islands or near Nerano, then crosses to Capri in 45 to 60 minutes. The first part on Capri is a slow lap of the island from the water: the Faraglioni and their arch, the green and white grottoes, the Punta Carena lighthouse and the Blue Grotto, if the sea lets it open. Then you get two to four hours ashore at Marina Grande, enough for the funicular up to the Piazzetta and lunch. You are back in Positano between 5 and 6 in the afternoon.

Shared small-group tours cost about €95–170 per person in season. Drinks and snorkel masks are often included; lunch, the funicular and the Blue Grotto rowing boat (around €20, cash) are not. Full route map and our score: Capri boat tour from Positano.

Positano to Capri: tour, ferry or private boat?

OptionTypical costWhat you get

Public ferryaround €25–30 each wayFastest transfer, no lap of the island, no swim stops, fixed timetable

Shared boat tour€95–170 per personLap of Capri, Blue Grotto stop, swim stops, time ashore

Private gozzo€900–2,200 per boatSame sights at your pace; good value from about six people

If you only want a day walking around Capri town and Anacapri, the ferry is enough. If you want to see the island from the sea and swim, the tour is the better day. Fares and prices change by season: check them for your dates.

Tips

Book the Capri day for early in your stay so you have a spare day if the sea is rough. Pack cash for the Blue Grotto and the funicular, a hat and reef-safe sunscreen. If you are prone to seasickness, sit at the back of the boat and choose a morning departure, when the sea is usually calmer.

Frequently asked questions
How much is a boat tour from Positano to Capri?
A shared small-group Capri boat tour from Positano usually costs €95–170 per person. A private gozzo for the day is roughly €900–2,200 for the whole boat. The Blue Grotto entry is paid separately on the spot.
How long is the boat ride from Positano to Capri?
About 45 to 60 minutes in a typical tour boat, depending on the boat and the sea.
Can I go from Positano to Capri without a tour?
Yes, by public ferry in season. A tour adds the lap of the island and swim stops that the ferry does not.
Do Positano boat tours run in winter?
Very few. The season runs roughly from April to October.

Home / Guides / Boat tours from Amalfi
Boat tours from Amalfi

Amalfi is the eastern hub of the coast, ideal if you stay in Amalfi, Atrani, Ravello, Minori or Maiori.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

From Amalfi, take the shared Capri tour for a full classic day, or a private three to four hour cruise to the Emerald Grotto, Furore and Praiano if you prefer calm water and swimming.

Where boats leave from

Tours start from Amalfi harbour, next to the ferry piers on the seafront by Piazza Flavio Gioia. Guests from Ravello usually take a bus or taxi down, so allow for traffic in summer.

Capri from Amalfi

The crossing to Capri is longer than from Positano or Sorrento, roughly an hour and a half each way, but you see the entire coast on the way. Shared tours make it a long but rich day. See route. On a private boat, a speedboat makes the distance much easier.

The coast from Amalfi

The stretch between Amalfi and Positano holds the coast's best sights by sea: the Emerald Grotto, the Furore fjord and the beaches of Praiano. A private half-day cruise covers it comfortably and can include Positano from the water.

Tips

If Capri is your priority and you have flexibility, consider starting from Positano to gain an hour on the island. Amalfi tours are often less crowded than Positano ones in July and August.

How far is Capri from Amalfi by boat?
Around 35 km of sea, about 75 to 90 minutes on a tour boat and faster on a speedboat.
Can I visit the Emerald Grotto by boat from Amalfi?
Yes, many private and some shared boats stop there. Entry into the grotto itself is a separate ticket.
Is Ravello a good base for boat tours?

Home / Guides / Boat tours from Sorrento
Boat tours from Sorrento

Sorrento has the most departures and the shortest crossing to Capri.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

From Sorrento, a shared Capri tour gives the most island time for the money. If you want to see the Amalfi Coast itself, take the boat day to Positano and Amalfi instead of the coast road.

Where boats leave from

Most tours leave from Marina Piccola, below the town centre, reached by stairs or a lift from the Villa Comunale. Some include hotel pickups along the Sorrento peninsula.

Two very different days

Capri is under an hour away, so a Sorrento Capri tour spends more time around the island. The Amalfi Coast is on the other side of the peninsula: a boat day to Positano and Amalfi rounds Punta Campanella and avoids the slow coast road.

Which first?

If you only have one day, most people choose Capri. With two, do both, Capri first in case you need a spare day for weather.

Tips

Sorrento has many operators, so compare group size and inclusions carefully. Check whether the Punta Campanella marine reserve and the Bay of Ieranto are on the route: they are some of the most beautiful swim spots in the area.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/capri-blue-grotto-boat-tour/

Home / Guides / Capri & the Blue Grotto by boat
Capri and the Blue Grotto by boat

The Blue Grotto is the most famous sight on Capri and the most misunderstood.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

No boat tour can enter the Blue Grotto itself. Tours stop outside and you transfer to a small rowing boat, paying a separate fee on the spot. It closes when the sea is rough, so treat it as a bonus, not the reason for the trip.

How entry works

The entrance is a hole in the rock about a metre high. Visitors move from their tour boat into small rowing boats holding a few people, lie back as the rower pulls through on a chain, and spend a few minutes inside the glowing blue cave. The fee for the rowing boat and the entry is paid there, in recent seasons around €20 per person. Bring cash and check the current price.

When it closes

Even a moderate swell makes the entrance unsafe, so the grotto closes regularly, sometimes for days in spring and autumn. It is generally open from morning to late afternoon in calm conditions. Early in the day queues are shorter and the sea is usually calmer.

Queues

In July and August the wait at sea can exceed an hour. Private boats can time it better; shared tours decide on the day whether waiting is worth it.

Which tour to choose

- Staying on the coast: a Capri boat tour from Positano, Amalfi or Sorrento.

- Already on Capri: the island tour from Marina Grande.

- Want the best chance: a private boat with an early start.

Beyond the Blue Grotto

The Faraglioni rocks, the arch you can sail through, the green and white grottoes and the coves near Punta Carena are often more memorable than the Blue Grotto itself, and they are on every island lap.

Can you swim in the Blue Grotto?
No. Swimming inside is not allowed during opening hours.
Is the Blue Grotto worth it?
In calm weather and without a long queue, yes: the light is extraordinary. With a long wait, many visitors prefer more swim time elsewhere.
Can children enter the Blue Grotto?
Yes, children travel in the rowing boats with their parents.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/amalfi-coast-boat-tour-with-kids/

Home / Guides / Boat tours with kids
Amalfi Coast boat tours with kids

Children usually love the boat and hate the waiting. Pick a format with short legs, shade and somewhere to swim.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

With children under about eight, choose a private boat for three to four hours along the coast (about €450–900 for the whole boat) or a two hour sunset cruise (€50–95 per person). From about nine, most children enjoy a full Capri day, ideally on a small-group or private boat with shade.

Best options by age

AgeBest choice

Babies and toddlersShort private coast cruise or sunset cruise

4–8 yearsPrivate half day, or Capri island tour if already on Capri

9+ yearsFull-day Capri tour, private if budget allows

How long is too long?

A full Capri day means seven to eight hours, with close to two hours of sailing in total. That works for most children from about nine who like the water. Younger ones usually do best with two to four hours and a swim in the middle. The giveaway is waiting time: queues at the Blue Grotto and crowded Marina Grande wear children out faster than the sea does.

Kid-friendly boat trips by where you stay

- Positano: the sunset cruise to Li Galli is short and calm, a good first boat trip. For a longer day, a private coast cruise lets you stop at a quiet cove whenever someone needs a swim or a snack.

- Amalfi: a private half day to the Emerald Grotto and the Furore fjord stays in sheltered water close to the shore. Route and prices.

- Sorrento: Capri is under an hour away, the shortest crossing on the coast, so a Capri tour from Sorrento is the easiest full day with older kids.

- Already on Capri: the one to two hour island tour from Marina Grande is a gentle option for any age.

What to ask the operator

- Are there life jackets in children's sizes?
- Does the boat have a shade canopy?
- Is there a toilet on board? (Small gozzo boats usually do not.)
- Can the plan be shortened if a child is unwell?

Seasickness

Mornings are generally calmer. Sit at the back, look at the horizon, avoid heavy breakfasts. Ask a pharmacist about remedies suitable for your child's age before the trip.

What to pack

Hats, swim shirts, reef-safe sunscreen, water, snacks, a change of clothes, a towel and swim shoes for pebble beaches.

Why private boats often make sense

For a family of four or five the price gap narrows, and the freedom to stop, swim and turn back is what makes the day work with kids.

Frequently asked questions
Are boat tours on the Amalfi Coast safe for babies?
Short trips in calm water are generally fine. Bring an infant life jacket if the operator does not have one, and keep the trip short.
Do children pay full price?
Policies vary. Shared tours often discount children; private boats charge per boat, not per person.
What is the best family boat tour from Positano?
A private three to four hour cruise along the coast, or the sunset cruise for younger children.
What age is good for a Capri boat tour?
Most children from about nine cope well with a full Capri day. Younger children can do it on a private boat that can shorten the plan, but a half day on the coast is usually happier for everyone.
Is there a toilet on Amalfi Coast tour boats?
Larger tour boats and yachts usually have one, small wooden gozzo boats usually do not. Ask before booking if you travel with young children.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/amalfi-coast-boat-tour-prices/

Home / Guides / Boat tour prices
How much does an Amalfi Coast boat tour cost?

Typical price ranges across listings, what is included and the extras people forget.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

Shared full-day tours to Capri usually cost €80–180 per person. Private boats cost around €450–1,500 for the coast and €900–2,200 for a full day to Capri, per boat. Short sunset cruises are about €50–95 per person.

Typical ranges

TourTypical price

Capri island tour from Marina Grande€20–45 per person

Positano sunset cruise€50–95 per person

Shared Capri tour from Sorrento€80–150 per person

Shared Capri tour from Positano€95–170 per person

Shared Capri tour from Amalfi€100–180 per person

Private coast cruise (3–8 h)€450–1,500 per boat

Private boat to Capri (full day)€900–2,200 per boat

Ranges are indicative and move with season, date and boat. Always check the live price for your date.

Private boat price per person

Private boats are priced per boat, so the cost per head falls quickly as the group grows. A coast cruise at €600 is €300 each for a couple and €100 each for six people. A Capri day at €1,400 is €700 each for two and about €175 each for eight, close to a shared tour. For two people, a private boat is a treat for a special day; from six people it is often the better deal.

Water taxi and private transfers

A water taxi on the Amalfi Coast is a private boat that takes you from one town to another, for example Positano to Amalfi or to a beach club, with no stops on the way. It is priced per boat, roughly €100–300 for short hops along the coast and more for Capri, depending on distance, boat and season. Public ferries between Positano, Amalfi and Capri are much cheaper per person but follow a timetable and stop running in the evening and in rough sea.

Boat rental without a skipper

In Italy you can rent a small motorboat (up to 40 hp) without a licence. Expect roughly €150–350 for a day in season, with fuel usually extra. It is the cheapest way to have a boat to yourself, but you plan the route, handle the anchoring and cannot go far: Capri is generally too far for these boats. With children or little boating experience, a boat with a skipper is the safer choice.

What drives the price

- Season: July and August are the most expensive; May, June and September offer the best balance.

- Distance: Capri from Amalfi uses more fuel than from Sorrento.

- Boat: gozzo, speedboat or yacht.
- Group size: small groups cost more than large boats.

Extras to budget

Blue Grotto entry (paid on the spot), Capri funicular, lunch ashore, Emerald Grotto ticket, tips for the crew, and on private boats possibly fuel and port fees.

How to save

Travel in the shoulder season, start from Sorrento for Capri, share a private boat with friends, and book refundable options early before the best boats sell out.

Frequently asked questions
How much is a private boat tour for two people on the Amalfi Coast?
A private boat costs the same whether you are two or eight: roughly €450–1,500 for a coast cruise and €900–2,200 for a full day to Capri. For two people a shared tour (€80–180 each) is far cheaper.
How much does a water taxi cost on the Amalfi Coast?
Roughly €100–300 per boat for a short private transfer between towns, more for Capri. Prices depend on distance, boat and season.
Is it cheaper to book boat tours locally in Positano?
Sometimes on the day, but in high season the best boats sell out. Booking online with free cancellation secures a place.
Do you tip on a boat tour in Italy?
Not mandatory. On private boats 5 to 10 percent for a great skipper is appreciated.
Are drinks included?
Usually water and soft drinks, often prosecco or limoncello. Lunch is rarely included on shared Capri tours.

# https://amalficoastboatguide.com/guides/best-time-for-amalfi-coast-boat-tour/

Home / Guides / When to go
Best time for an Amalfi Coast boat tour

Boats run from about April to October, but May and September are a different experience from August.

Updated November 2026 · By the Amalfi Coast Boat Guide team

Late May, June and September are the sweet spot: warm water, long days and fewer crowds than July and August. Book a morning departure for calmer sea.

Month by month

MonthWhat to expect

AprilSeason starts, cool water, fewer departures, greener cliffs.

MayPleasant days, water still fresh for swimming, good prices.

JuneLong days, warm water, busy but manageable. Our favourite.

July–AugustHottest, warmest sea, highest prices, crowded Capri and Blue Grotto queues.

SeptemberWarm sea, softer light, crowds easing. Excellent.

OctoberStill possible, shorter days, more weather cancellations.

November–MarchVery few tours; private boats on request in good weather.

Time of day

Mornings are usually calmer. Afternoon breezes can make the return choppy. For photos, the late afternoon light on Positano is the best of the day.

Weather and cancellations

Skippers cancel when the sea is unsafe; reputable operators rebook or refund. Book your boat day early in your stay and choose listings with free cancellation so a rough day costs you nothing.

Booking ahead

For June to September, book two to six weeks ahead for the best small-group and private boats. For May 2027 departures, prices and availability are already live on the partner sites.

Frequently asked questions
What is the sea temperature on the Amalfi Coast?
Roughly 18 °C in May, 23 °C in June, 25–26 °C in August and 23–24 °C in September.
What happens if my boat tour is cancelled for weather?
You are normally offered a new date or a refund. Check the cancellation terms before booking.
Is October too late for a boat tour?
Not necessarily: many days are calm and warm, but keep a spare day in case of cancellation.
